book: Quantitative Aptitude for Competitive Examinations — R.S. Aggarwal

key_explanation_from_book.race_ratio: If A beats B by x metres in a race of d metres, then A : B = d : (d-x).
key_explanation_from_book.three_racers: For three contestants, combine pairwise speed ratios to obtain the ratio between the required two contestants.
key_explanation_from_book.start: A start means the distance or points by which one contestant is allowed to begin ahead of another.
key_explanation_from_book.points_games: The same ratio method used for races is applied to games measured in points. If A can give B a points start, compare their effective scores to obtain their speed/playing-strength ratio.
key_explanation_from_book.same_time: When two contestants reach the winning post at the same time, the distance each actually travels is proportional to their speeds.
key_explanation_from_book.speed_conversion: For speed calculations involving km/hr and m/sec, use 1 km/hr = 5/18 m/sec.
